set.title: Settings
set.beam_hint: default 5 · above ~10 hardly any gain, higher = much slower
set.compute_hint: float16 = much faster with practically the same accuracy
set.batch_hint: speed only, no effect on the result · 8–16 is reasonable
set.device_hint: cuda = graphics card · cpu only as a fallback
set.numerals: Write numbers as words (exact timestamps, but no digits)
set.note_whisper: Changes on this tab reload the model on the next start. A separate model for one language is set under “Languages”.
set.onset_hint: start of speech · lower = more sensitive
set.offset_hint: end of speech · lower = speech is held longer
set.chunk_hint: maximum length of a chunk · matters mostly in raw mode
set.note_vad: For speeches with background noise, slightly lower values than the default often work better (e.g. 0.4 / 0.323). Too low: noise is detected as speech.
set.gap_enabled: Gap check: report loud passages without text after each transcription
set.sw_score: Score check: mark words with a score below
set.orphan_fill: Short words after a comma: fill level (percent)
set.balance_lines: Balance lines: spread the words evenly over the lines
set.line_gap: Gap to the next song line (seconds)
set.note_subs: Characters per line and lines per subtitle are set in the main window and saved there with “Save as default”.

set.encoding_hint: utf-8-sig if a player shows special characters wrongly

set.ui_language_hint: restart needed · “like Windows” = system language, otherwise English
set.dnd_restart: installed – active after restarting the window
set.note_start: Language, mode, audio filter, layout and prompt preselection are saved in the main window with “Save as default”.

no_cues: {label}: no subtitles found – is this an SRT file?
rep.missing_title: Nothing at this point in this file
rep.diff_intro_ab: Colored = only in this file · “missing” = nothing at this point there.
rep.diff_intro_ref: The green Ref line shows what is correct.
rep.diff_intro_noref: Without a reference this does not show who is right – click the time and listen.
rep.diff_intro_ar: Blue = as in A · green = as in the reference · “missing” = nothing there.
rep.shared_intro: Blue-purple = as in A and in B · green = what would be correct. A different beam or model often does not change these errors – the prompt (names/terms) and replacements help here.
rep.short_word: Short word – check that it is never correct elsewhere
rep.sg_intro: Derived from the reference: what was recognized → what is correct. Only take over if the wrong word is never correct elsewhere (typically names and terms). Target: Settings → Languages → Replacements.
rep.sg_none_multi: No error occurred more than once.
rep.sg_once: Misrecognized once – {n} (often chance, but useful for names)
rep.fmt_title: Spelling only – {places} (punctuation, upper/lower case – not counted as errors)
rep.full_legend: {wx} only in {x} · {wy} only in {y} · {wf} different spelling (hover shows {x})
rep.timing_line: typically {typ} off · {offset} · {pct} of words more than {s}
rep.timing_none: No passage with too large a deviation.
rep.timing_note_ref: Note: the reference times only count if they were checked – if the reference was corrected from A, A automatically looks good.
rep.timing_explain: The times of identical words are compared. SRTs only have times per cue, the time of each word is estimated within it – that is why only deviations over {s} count, and only if at least {n} words in a row are affected.
rep.col_wer_title: Share of wrong words within the reference range
rep.col_sub_title: wrong word instead of the correct one
rep.col_del_title: word of the reference is missing
rep.col_ins_title: word that does not occur in the reference
rep.col_typ_title: Typical timing deviation of identical words from the reference (median of the differences)
rep.col_offset_title: Offset: signed median – plus = later than the reference, minus = earlier
rep.col_off_title: Share of words that are more than {s} away from the reference
rep.col_punct_title: Words with punctuation at the end
rep.banner_best: is more accurate: {wer_w} instead of {wer_l} errors – {n_w} instead of {n_l} wrong words ({less} fewer).
rep.banner_shared: A and B share {n} of these errors (see “Errors in both”) – the difference between A and B does not change them.
rep.banner_a: {wer} errors compared to the reference – {n} of {words} words.
rep.banner_noref: Without a reference the report only shows where A and B differ – not who is right. For that, add a corrected SRT as reference (5–10 minutes are enough).
rep.ref_span: Error rate only within the reference range: {t0} – {t1} ({n} words).
rep.listen_hint: click a time – plays from 1.5 s before
rep.play_error: The file cannot be played here (moved or format not supported).
rep.intro: Only the plain text counts – timestamps, numbers and line breaks do not matter.
rep.colors: Same colors everywhere: {a} blue · {b} purple · {r} green (correct).

files: • Lyrics – <name>.lyric.txt is next to it, the song text is only aligned in time
• JSON → SRT – a saved WhisperX result is only converted into subtitles again
Status “⚠ gaps”: loud passages without text were found – details in the log
Status “⚠ unsure”: words with a low score (score check) – details in the log
Double-click: show the finished SRT in Explorer
Start processes the selected files, otherwise all open ones.
add: Whole folders: drag them onto the BAT or – with drag & drop enabled – directly into the list.
compare: Compares two SRT files word by word – timestamps, numbers and line breaks do not matter.

Result: an HTML report in the browser with all word differences and their time positions (to listen to), differences in punctuation/case only and – with a corrected reference – the error rate of both files.
If a file is selected, its SRTs are suggested.
tip.cmp_a: First version, e.g. created with the standard model. Always blue in the report.
cmp_b: Second version, e.g. created with a fine-tuned model or a different beam. Always purple in the report.
Optional if a reference is given – the report then shows the errors of A alone.
cmp_media: Optional: the video or audio of the speech. Then all times in the report are clickable and play the passage (from 1.5 s before) – so you immediately hear who is right.
The tool puts a small audio track (.m4a) next to the report that every browser can play – whatever the video format of the source.
cmp_ref: Optional: a manually corrected SRT of the same recording (e.g. improved in Subtitle Edit).

Then the report shows at every point who is right, calculates the error rate (WER) for A and B, lists errors that both make and suggests replacements – the most objective comparison. Always green in the report. Even 5–10 corrected minutes are enough for a good assessment.
tip.remove: Remove selected files from the list (the files themselves stay unchanged). Also with the Del key.
tip.clear: Clear the list (the files themselves stay unchanged).
tip.folder: Opens the folder of the selected (or first) file in Explorer.
lang: Automatic: Whisper listens to the first 30 seconds and decides for the whole file – anew for each file. Risky if the start contains music, applause, an intro or a quote in another language: then the whole file is transcribed in the wrong language.
Fixed: more reliable. Applies to all files of this run – so split mixed batches by language.
The language also determines prompt, filler words, dangling words and replacements (Settings → Languages).
mode: Sentences: subtitles by sentence, with character limit and the orphan, dangling and pause rules – for normal subtitles.
Word by word: every word is its own subtitle – for karaoke or highlight effects in the video editor.
Raw: the WhisperX segments unchanged (often long, up to 30 s) – as raw text or when there are no word timestamps.
chars: Maximum characters per line (sentences mode only). The line is filled up to exactly this value.
tip.lines: Maximum lines per subtitle (sentences mode only). 1–2 is usual; more than 2 cover a lot of the picture.
filter: FFmpeg audio filter before transcription (speech only, lyrics stay unfiltered).
On: helps with reverb, street noise, hum and quiet speakers.
Off: for clean recordings often just as good or better – Whisper itself is fairly robust against noise.
Which filters run and what they do: Settings → Audio & output.
json: Also saves the WhisperX result as <name>.json.
Later drag the .json into the tool → new SRT with a different layout, other replacements or rules in seconds, without a new transcription.
hold: Lyrics only: extend the end of a line by up to this many seconds – but never beyond the start of the next line.
The alignment often ends before the note fades; then the line disappears too early.
save_defaults: Saves the current selection of this area as default in the INI: language, mode, chars/lines, audio filter, JSON, hold line and prompt choice (incl. custom text).
The next time the window opens, this is preselected.
pmode_ini: Takes the prompt of the language from Settings → Languages.
With “Automatic” the prompt of the detected language.
pmode_custom: Custom prompt for this run (permanently with “Save as default”).
Tips: write in the language of the audio, keep it short, write names and terms exactly as they should appear in the subtitle. The prompt also influences style and punctuation.
tip.pmode_none: Without prompt – for comparison, or when the prompt causes errors (e.g. prompt words appear as text in silence or music).
prompt_field: The prompt is a hint to Whisper: it makes rare names and terms more likely and sets style and spelling.
WhisperX puts it in front of every chunk. If it is too long, only the last ~220 tokens count – the beginning is dropped.
start: Starts processing: selected files – otherwise all still open – otherwise all again (e.g. with a different layout).
The models stay loaded as long as the window is open; the second run starts without loading time.
tip.cancel: Cancels after the current step. A running transcription cannot be stopped in the middle.
tip.settings: Less frequently changed settings: model, precision, speech detection (VAD), subtitle rules, audio filter, prompts and replacements per language, interface language, system check, drag & drop.
log: gray time + white text = lines recognized live
yellow = warning · red = error · green = done · blue = new file
Text can be selected and copied with Ctrl+C.
model: large-v2: predecessor – sometimes invents less text in silence or music.
large-v3-turbo: much faster (heavily reduced decoder), somewhat less accurate.
“Folder …”: own model in CTranslate2 format, e.g. a fine-tune. The folder must contain model.bin and preprocessor_config.json, among others.
Graphics memory for large: about 3–5 GB in float16, about 6–8 GB in float32.
beam: Beam search: Whisper follows this many candidate sentences at the same time and takes the most likely one.
40 costs many times the time and graphics memory
compute: Computing precision on the graphics card:
float16 – half precision, much faster on RTX cards, practically identical result
float32 – full precision, slower, twice the graphics memory
int8_float16 – less graphics memory, minimally less accurate
int8 – for running on the CPU
batch: How many chunks (up to 30 s) are decoded at the same time on the graphics card.
Only affects speed, not the result – WhisperX processes every chunk independently.
Higher = faster, needs more graphics memory. With 12–16 GB of graphics memory, 8–16 is reasonable.
device: cpu = processor – always works, but is many times slower.
numerals: Suppresses digits and symbols: Whisper writes “sixth of November” instead of “6 November”, “fifty percent” instead of “50%”.
Advantage: every number gets an exact word timestamp (the alignment model does not know digits).
Disadvantage: no digits in the subtitle.
vad_method: VAD = voice activity detection: finds the passages with speech – only these are transcribed. Silence, music and noise in between are skipped. This prevents invented text and saves time.
pyannote – WhisperX default. Neural segmentation model, sets speech boundaries precisely, robust against background noise.
silero – small, very fast model with its own detection. Try it if pyannote swallows quiet speech or detects applause/music as speech.
onset: Threshold (0–1) from which a chunk begins as speech.
Lower (e.g. 0.35–0.45): quiet or distant speakers are captured – but also more noise.
Higher (0.5–0.7): only clear speech, fewer false starts.
offset: Threshold (0–1) below which the speech probability must fall for a chunk to end.
Lower: chunks are held longer – word endings and short pauses are not cut off.
WhisperX default: 0.363 · should be below the onset
tip.vad_defaults: Sets the WhisperX defaults: pyannote, onset 0.500, offset 0.363, chunk length 30 s.
chunk: Detected speech pieces are merged into chunks up to this length. Whisper works in 30-second windows, so at most 30.
Smaller (10–20): shorter raw segments, sometimes more precise times; too small can cut sentences.
Usually irrelevant for sentences and word-by-word modes.
gap_enabled: Gap check after each transcription: looks for passages that are loud and voice-like but got no text – typical when speech detection (VAD) swallows quiet speech or Whisper skips a sentence.
How it works: level clearly above the noise floor AND a sound with fundamental and overtones (voice) instead of broadband noise (applause, wind, traffic).
Findings appear in yellow in the log, the file gets “⚠ gaps” as status. It is a hint to check: music, singing or chanting can also be reported. Takes about 5 s per 2 h of audio.
gap_srt: Also saves the findings as <name>{suffix}. Load it as a second subtitle track in VLC or Subtitle Edit – then you jump directly to the suspicious passages.
If there are no gaps any more, an old {suffix} is removed automatically.
gap_min: Only report gaps of at least this length. Shorter passages are mostly breaths, laughs or heckling.
gap_margin: How clearly a passage must be above the noise floor of the recording to count as “loud”.
Smaller (5–6): also finds very quiet speakers, but more false alarms.
score: Score check after each transcription: the word timestamps give every word a score from 0 to 1 – how well it fits the audio at its place. Clearly recognized words are high (often 0.8–1.0). A low score means the word was probably misrecognized or misplaced.
Words below the threshold are marked. A higher threshold gives more entries. Recommended: 0.40.
Names and foreign words land below it more often, even when they are right. Numbers are practically never marked; words with fewer than 3 letters are not rated.
Findings appear in yellow in the log, the file gets “⚠ unsure” as status. The subtitles themselves do not change.
score_srt: Also saves the findings as <name>{score_suffix}. Load it as a second subtitle track in VLC or Subtitle Edit – then you jump directly to the unsure words.
If there are no findings any more, an old {score_suffix} is removed automatically.
orphan_limit: A short word right after a comma starts the next subtitle instead of hanging alone at the end of a full line:
“… in Berlin, and” | “we see …”  →  “… in Berlin,” | “and we see …”
Applies to words up to this length.
tip.orphan_fill: … but only if the line is already at least this full (in percent of characters per line). Prevents very short subtitles.
max_duration: Long sentences are split: a subtitle holds at most this many seconds of speech, then a new one begins.
This is not a display time – how long a subtitle stays on screen is set under “2 · Display time”.
balance_lines: Spreads the words of a subtitle evenly over its lines instead of filling the first line to the limit:
“we did not see that / coming”  →  “we did not / see that coming”
Prefers a break after a comma and avoids an article or preposition at the end of a line. Same words, same number of lines – the times do not change.
line_gap: Song lines: gap to the next line when “Lyrics: hold line” (main window) extends the end – so that two lines visibly change.
0 = the lines follow each other seamlessly, without flicker – e.g. for DaVinci Resolve.
tip.ffmpeg: Path to ffmpeg.exe. ffmpeg reads any audio and video file, converts it to 16 kHz mono and applies the audio filter – directly into memory, without temp files.
filter_string: FFmpeg filter chain, parts separated by commas. The original filter:
Cuts everything below 100 Hz: footfall, hum, wind rumble. The voice lies above.
Cuts above 8.2 kHz. Whisper works with 16 kHz (usable up to 8 kHz) – so this part has practically no effect.
FFT noise reduction: lowers steady background noise (fans, hiss). With strong settings “bubbly” artifacts appear that rather disturb Whisper – if in doubt, compare with and without.
Dynamic loudness normalization: raises quiet passages without overdriving loud ones. f = window length in ms · g = smoothing (number of windows, odd) · p = target peak level · m = maximum gain.
Other useful filters: loudnorm (loudness per EBU R128), anlmdn (stronger noise reduction, slow).
Do not use: silenceremove, atempo – they shift the timestamps.
speech_suffix: Suffix of the subtitle file for speech: <name> + suffix. An existing file with the same name is overwritten.
Example .{model}.srt → speech.large-v3.srt or speech.whisper-large-v3-turkish-general.srt – so every model gets its own SRT, ideal for comparing (“Compare …” in the file list).
tip.lyrics_input: If <name> + this suffix is next to the media file, the song text is aligned instead of transcribed (lyrics mode). One song line per line, UTF-8.
tip.lyrics_suffix: Suffix of the lyrics subtitles: <name> + suffix.
encoding: utf-8 – default, works with all current programs.
utf-8-sig – with a marker (BOM) at the start of the file. Needed if an older player or program shows umlauts, Turkish or Arabic characters wrongly.
tip.lang_select: Which language is edited. “All languages” only contains replacements that apply in every language.
lang_prompt: Prompt for this language – always write it in this language. A German prompt with Turkish audio can tempt Whisper to translate.
Good: a short sentence about the content plus a list of rare names and terms in the desired spelling.
Too long: only the last ~220 tokens count.
Risk: in silence or music, prompt words sometimes appear as text – then shorten it.
lang_filler: Filler words that are removed in sentences and word-by-word modes – comma-separated, case does not matter.
If a filler word ends with a period (“uh.”), the end of the sentence is kept.
lang_dangling: Words that should never stand alone at the end of a subtitle (articles, prepositions) – they move to the start of the next one.
Exception: with punctuation (“I agree to.”) or before a long pause they stay.
lang_abbrev: Abbreviations that stay with the next word and never end a sentence, comma-separated: “Dr. Smith”, “e.g. Monday” are never split – not into two lines, not into two subtitles.
Write multi-part ones the way Whisper writes them (“e. g.” and “e.g.” are different). Ordinal numbers like “6.” in German and Turkish always stay with the next word.
Not included on purpose: etc. – it often ends a sentence.
lang_repl: Corrections for recurring misrecognitions, one per line:
Only whole words and phrases are replaced: “Maier” becomes “Meier”, “Maierhofer” stays untouched.
Case does not matter when searching; exactly the right-hand side is inserted.
Several words too: Open AI = OpenAI
Lines starting with ; or # are ignored.
lang_model: Optionally a separate model just for this language, e.g. a Turkish fine-tune in CTranslate2 format.

Enter it as a folder (“Folder …”) or directly as a Hugging Face name owner/model – then it is downloaded on first use (internet needed). The folder must contain model.bin and preprocessor_config.json; the system check shows whether it fits.
If the language changes between two files, the model is reloaded – sorting batches by language saves time.
tip.timeout: Seconds until the automatic start when files were dropped onto the BAT. A click into the window stops it. 0 = never start automatically.
tip.skip: Starts immediately without countdown – handy if the defaults always fit.
tip.live: Shows every recognized line in the log already during transcription – like in a console window.
tip.check: Checks Python, all required packages with versions, ffmpeg and the graphics card (CUDA). Also runs automatically every time the window starts.
dnd: Dragging files directly into the list needs the small package tkinterdnd2 (no further dependencies).
It is installed with --no-deps: only this one package, nothing else in the venv is changed. Then restart the window.
tip.ini_open: Opens whisper_tool.ini in the default editor – with all comments.
ui_language: Language of the interface, the log and the comparison report.
“like Windows”: uses the system language if there is a language file for it, otherwise English.
More languages: copy lang/en.json, translate it and save it as lang/<code>.json – it then appears in this list automatically.
pause: The limit between a short and a real pause. Only the length of the pause counts – in the middle of a sentence or between two sentences.
Up to this length: a short pause. Longer: a real pause, e.g. applause, thinking or music.
After a real pause a new segment always begins, in every mode: Sentences and Raw are split there; in Word by word every word is its own segment anyway. Recommended: 2 seconds.
smooth: For programs that show nothing for a moment between two subtitles and therefore flicker – e.g. the subtitle track of DaVinci Resolve.
Short pause: the segment stays until the next one starts – end and next start are exactly the same.
Real pause: the segment stays for the set time, then the screen is empty until speech starts again.
A segment is what is shown: a word in word by word mode, a subtitle in sentence mode. Starts stay exact – every word appears exactly when it is spoken.
Without the tick the SRT is exactly as spoken, e.g. for the comparison report. Lyrics have their own rules (3 · Lyrics). Recommended: hold time 1 second.
tip.resolve_install: Copies the plugin into DaVinci Resolve's script folder (…\Fusion\Scripts\Utility). The folder of this Workbench, the interface language and all texts of the plugin are written into it – there is nothing to configure. Install it again after moving the Workbench or changing the language.
tip.resolve_countdown: Seconds until a job from DaVinci Resolve is transcribed automatically. A click into the window stops the countdown.
tip.resolve_hand_over: Moves the subtitles to the position of the transcribed range in the timeline and hands them to the waiting plugin in DaVinci Resolve. The SRT is read again from disk – changes made in the meantime count.
tip.resolve_auto_hand_over: No need to press “Hand over to DaVinci”: as soon as the job is transcribed, the subtitles go to the waiting plugin. Useful when you check the subtitles in Resolve anyway.
tip.resolve_track_gaps: An extra subtitle track in Resolve: “WhisperX gaps” marks loud passages without text. Needs the gap check (tab Speech detection). It is for checking – delete the track afterwards. Nothing is added when there is nothing to show.
tip.resolve_track_fast: An extra subtitle track in Resolve: “WhisperX too fast” marks subtitles with more than 17 characters per second. Mode “Sentences” only. It is for checking – delete the track afterwards. Nothing is added when there is nothing to show.
resolve_score: An extra subtitle track in Resolve: “WhisperX unsure” marks words with a low score (score check). This is the same setting as on the tab Speech detection – a change shows up in both places.

The score ranges from 0 to 1; clearly recognized words are high. A higher threshold gives more entries. Names and foreign words land below it more often. Numbers are practically never marked; words with fewer than 3 letters are not rated.
It is for checking – delete the track afterwards. Nothing is added when there is nothing to show.
tip.resolve_close_after: Without the tick the Workbench minimizes itself after the hand-over and keeps its models loaded – the next job starts without loading time. With the tick it closes.
